recommendation: Keep the source fix. Do not add proposed/planned lifecycle status codes for this issue; current planned/proposed semantics belong in intent unless a future work-group decision reopens the workflow pattern.
issue_request: FHIR-3720 was a Published/Persuasive with Modification DSTU1 Patient Care issue asking request/order classes to support planned and proposed activities, originally via status values on resources such as CarePlan, DiagnosticRequest, MedicationPrescription, ReferralRequest, and NutritionOrder.
initial_application: The explicit #3720 application was git d6259fa8e3beda8fd5e58ad54d85001f1efb9d42, which added proposed/planned to then-current DiagnosticOrder and NutritionOrder status lists. Later resource refactors replaced or subsumed several original artifacts: DiagnosticOrder and ReferralRequest into ServiceRequest, and MedicationPrescription into MedicationRequest.
additional_context: Current FHIR source separates lifecycle status from request authority: Request.status is lifecycle-oriented, while Request.intent carries proposal, plan, and order semantics. FHIR-9266 later declined adding proposed/planned to MedicationOrder status because it follows the Request workflow pattern, and FHIR-14414 added NutritionOrder intent/status alignment to that pattern. Current CarePlan, ServiceRequest, MedicationRequest, and NutritionOrder definitions already support proposal/plan/order through intent, but NutritionOrder.status still contained stale wording for an invalid requested status and receiver-maintained fulfillment.
reconciliation: Updated source/nutritionorder/structuredefinition-NutritionOrder.xml and the matching nutritionorder-request-mapping-exceptions.xml entry to remove the invalid requested-status/receiver-maintained wording and state that NutritionOrder.status reflects requester-controlled lifecycle state, with performer fulfillment status represented by events or Task.
source_changes: source/nutritionorder/structuredefinition-NutritionOrder.xml: replaced stale NutritionOrder.status comment that referenced requested status and receiver-managed updates with requester-controlled lifecycle status wording.
source/nutritionorder/nutritionorder-request-mapping-exceptions.xml: updated the corresponding Request.status mapping exception resource comment to match the corrected NutritionOrder.status prose.
